category: Phrasal verbs on regular bases: A-C

entries.meaning: To do something because of advice, information, or an order you have been given. ---
examples: We act on every complaint we get.
The police acted on an anonymous tip.
He's finally acting on his doctor's advice.
entries.русский: действовать по (совету, информации); принимать меры, принять меры
entries.separable: inseparable — act on the advice, never act the advice on
entries.forms: act on · acted on · acted on

entries.meaning: To behave badly because of feelings you cannot put into words. ---
examples: Kids often act out when their parents separate.
He acted out for months after the move.
The counselor says she's acting out, not turning mean.
entries.русский: срываться, сорваться; выплёскивать эмоции в плохом поведении
entries.separable: no object — he's acting out; in this meaning the verb stands alone
entries.forms: act out · acted out · acted out

entries.meaning: To perform something as a scene, showing it with actions instead of telling it. ---
examples: The kids act out the whole story with puppets.
She acted out the argument for us, doing both voices.
They were acting out the scene when the lights went out.
entries.separable: separable — act out the scene, and act it out; a pronoun has to go in the middle
entries.forms: act out · acted out · acted out

entries.meaning: To behave badly, especially of a child who wants attention. ---
examples: The twins act up every time we have company.
He acted up in class all week and lost recess.
She's been acting up ever since the baby came home.
entries.separable: no object — the kids are acting up; nothing ever stands between act and up
entries.forms: act up · acted up · acted up

entries.meaning: To start working badly or hurting, of a machine or a part of the body. ---
examples: My knee acts up when it rains.
The printer acted up again this morning.
The old furnace has been acting up all winter.
entries.русский: барахлить, забарахлить; давать сбои; ныть (о больном месте)
entries.separable: no object — the printer is acting up; the two words never come apart
entries.forms: act up · acted up · acted up

entries.meaning: To include something in a mixture, a list, or a total you are putting together. ---
examples: Add in the chocolate chips at the very end.
They added in two more names at the last minute.
Don't forget you're adding in tax and tip.
entries.separable: separable — add in the eggs, and add them in
entries.forms: add in · added in · added in

entries.meaning: To charge or include something extra, on top of what is already there. ---
examples: They add on a twenty percent service charge for big parties.
The dealer added on four hundred dollars in fees.
We're adding on a delivery charge starting in June.
entries.separable: separable — add on a service charge, and add it on
entries.forms: add on · added on · added on

entries.meaning: To find the total of a set of numbers. ---
examples: Add up the column and tell me what you get.
She added up the receipts twice.
I'm still adding up what the trip cost us.
entries.separable: separable — add up the numbers, and add them up
entries.forms: add up · added up · added up

entries.meaning: To grow into a large amount through many small ones. ---
examples: Three dollars a day doesn't sound like much, but it adds up.
The late fees added up fast.
Those extra hours have been adding up all month.
entries.separable: no object — the little charges add up
entries.forms: add up · added up · added up

entries.meaning: To make sense, said most often when something does not. ---
examples: His story just doesn't add up.
Nothing she told the police added up.
The numbers weren't adding up, so they ordered an audit.
entries.separable: no object — his story doesn't add up
entries.forms: add up · added up · added up

entries.meaning: To come to a total, or to amount to a particular result. ---
examples: The bills add up to almost two thousand dollars.
All that work added up to nothing.
Everything he's told us is adding up to one thing: he's quitting.
entries.русский: составлять, составить (в сумме); сводиться, свестись к
entries.separable: inseparable — all three words stay together and the total follows to: it adds up to nothing, never add it up to
entries.forms: add up to · added up to · added up to
entries.third person: adds up to · -ing form: adding up to

entries.meaning: To let fresh air into a room or through cloth to get rid of a smell or dampness. ---
examples: Open the windows and air out the bedroom.
She aired out the sleeping bags on the porch.
The basement has been airing out since Tuesday.
entries.separable: separable — air out the bedroom, and air it out
entries.forms: air out · aired out · aired out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (air out the closet), intransitive (let the tent air out)

entries.meaning: To increase something in force, volume, or excitement. ---
examples: They amp up security every year for the parade.
The coach amped up the pressure in the fourth quarter.
The ads are amping up the hype for the sequel.
entries.separable: separable — amp up the pressure, and amp it up
entries.forms: amp up · amped up · amped up

entries.meaning: To try to get something by hinting at it instead of asking straight out. ---
examples: He angles for a raise every time we talk.
They angled for a discount and got one.
She was angling for an invitation all evening.
entries.separable: inseparable — angle for a raise, never angle a raise for
entries.forms: angle for · angled for · angled for

entries.meaning: To reply rudely to someone who has authority over you. ---
examples: Don't answer back when your grandmother is talking.
He answered back and got sent to his room.
She's been answering back a lot lately.
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — answer me back, never answer back me; most often there is no object at all: don't answer back
entries.forms: answer back · answered back · answered back
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (don't answer me back), intransitive (don't answer back)

entries.meaning: To be responsible to a person or group who can judge what you do. ---
examples: I answer to the regional manager, not to you.
He answered to no one for years.
Everyone here is answering to the same board now.
entries.separable: inseparable — answer to the board, never answer the board to
entries.forms: answer to · answered to · answered to

entries.meaning: To pay the money you owe or the share that is expected of you. ---
examples: If you want in on the trip, ante up.
Each of us anted up fifty dollars.
The city is anteing up half the cost of the new field.
entries.русский: раскошеливаться, раскошелиться; вносить, внести свою долю
entries.separable: inseparable — ante up fifty dollars, never ante fifty dollars up; most often there is no object at all
entries.forms: ante up · anted up · anted up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (ante up fifty dollars), intransitive (everybody has to ante up)

entries.meaning: To ask how someone is, usually by asking a third person about them. ---
examples: Your mother asked after you at church.
He always asks after my father.
She was asking after the kids.
entries.русский: справляться, справиться (о здоровье, о делах кого-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — ask after your mother, never ask your mother after
entries.forms: ask after · asked after · asked after

entries.meaning: To ask several different people about something, hoping one of them knows. ---
examples: Let me ask around and see if anyone has a truck.
I asked around at work and nobody had heard of it.
She's been asking around about a good dentist.
entries.separable: no object — ask around; what you want to know follows about: ask around about a good dentist
entries.forms: ask around · asked around · asked around

entries.meaning: To behave in a way that makes trouble certain to come. ---
examples: Riding at night with no lights is asking for trouble.
Nobody felt sorry for him — he asked for it.
She had asked for trouble the moment she took that shortcut.
entries.separable: inseparable — the trouble follows the particle: asking for trouble, and in the fixed line you asked for it
entries.forms: ask for · asked for · asked for

entries.meaning: To say that you want someone to give you something. ---
examples: Ask for a receipt when you pay.
She asked for two more days to finish the drawings.
He's asking for a raise at the review tomorrow.
entries.separable: inseparable — ask for the check, never ✗ ask the check for; the person you ask goes before the particle: ask him for help
entries.forms: ask for · asked for · asked for

entries.meaning: To invite someone to go on a date. ---
examples: I'm going to ask her out this weekend.
He asked out a girl from his chemistry class.
She's been wanting to ask him out since September.
entries.separable: separable — ask out a coworker, and ask her out; with a pronoun it must split
entries.forms: ask out · asked out · asked out

entries.meaning: To invite someone to come to your home. ---
examples: Let's ask the neighbors over for burgers.
They asked us over on Sunday.
She's asking over a few people from work.
entries.русский: приглашать, пригласить в гости (к себе домой)
entries.separable: separable — ask over a few friends, and ask them over; with a pronoun it must split
entries.forms: ask over · asked over · asked over

entries.meaning: To deal with something that needs doing, or to take care of someone. ---
examples: I have a few things to attend to before we leave.
A nurse attended to him all night.
She's attending to the paperwork right now.
entries.separable: inseparable — attend to the details, never attend the details to
entries.forms: attend to · attended to · attended to

entries.meaning: To sell something at an auction, usually to clear it out or raise money. ---
examples: The school auctions off the donated quilts every spring.
They auctioned off his tools after he died.
The bank is auctioning off the building next month.
entries.русский: продавать, продать с аукциона; распродавать, распродать с молотка
entries.separable: separable — auction off the painting, and auction it off
entries.forms: auction off · auctioned off · auctioned off

entries.meaning: To come to a particular figure as an average, or to even out over time. ---
examples: It averages out to about thirty dollars a week.
The good months and the bad ones averaged out by December.
Once you've averaged out the bonuses, the pay is decent.
entries.русский: составлять, составить в среднем; выравниваться, выровняться
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — average out the scores, and average them out; with no object it stays whole and the figure follows to or at
entries.forms: average out · averaged out · averaged out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (average out the scores), intransitive (it averages out to thirty dollars a week)

entries.meaning: To stop insisting on something after someone opposes you. ---
examples: He never backs down in an argument.
The company backed down after the boycott.
She has refused to back down, even with the numbers against her.
entries.русский: отступать, отступить; идти на попятную, пойти на попятную
entries.separable: no object — nothing can come between back and down; what you give up on follows the particle: back down from a threat
entries.forms: back down · backed down · backed down

entries.meaning: To stop pressuring or crowding someone and move away. ---
examples: Back off and let him finish.
The dog backed off as soon as I stood up.
They have backed off their demand for an apology.
entries.separable: inseparable on the rare occasions it takes an object — back off the deadline, never ✗ back the deadline off; normally it takes none
entries.forms: back off · backed off · backed off
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (just back off), transitive (they backed off the demand)

entries.meaning: To withdraw from something you had agreed to do. ---
examples: They backed out two days before the closing.
He is backing out of the deal.
She has backed out of every plan we've made.
entries.русский: отказываться, отказаться (от сделки); идти на попятную
entries.separable: no object — what you withdraw from follows the particle: back out of the contract, never ✗ back the contract out
entries.forms: back out · backed out · backed out

entries.meaning: To move a vehicle or yourself backward. ---
examples: Back up a little — you're too close to the garage.
He backed the truck up to the loading dock.
She was backing up when she hit the mailbox.
entries.русский: сдавать назад, сдать назад; пятиться, попятиться
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — back the truck up, back up the truck; usually it takes none at all: back up a little
entries.forms: back up · backed up · backed up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (back up slowly), transitive (back the car up)

entries.meaning: To pile up and stop moving, the way traffic or water in a clogged drain does. ---
examples: Traffic backs up on this bridge every morning.
The kitchen sink backed up again.
The accident backed traffic up for six miles.
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — backed traffic up, backed up traffic; most often there is none: the drain backed up
entries.forms: back up · backed up · backed up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (traffic backs up), transitive (the wreck backed traffic up)

entries.meaning: To save a second copy of computer files in case the first is lost. ---
examples: Back up your files before the update.
I backed everything up to an external drive.
The laptop is backing up right now.
entries.русский: делать резервную копию, сделать резервную копию
entries.separable: separable — back up your photos, and back them up
entries.forms: back up · backed up · backed up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (back up the files), intransitive (the laptop is backing up)

entries.meaning: To support someone or confirm what they say. ---
examples: Will you back me up if she asks?
Nobody backed him up in the meeting.
Two witnesses have backed up her story.
entries.separable: separable — back up your claim, and back me up; with a pronoun it must split: ✗ back up me
entries.forms: back up · backed up · backed up

entries.meaning: To abandon a person or a plan at the last minute. ---
examples: He bailed on us an hour before dinner.
She bails on every plan we make.
I can't believe they're bailing on the trip.
entries.separable: inseparable — bail on your friends, never ✗ bail your friends on
entries.forms: bail on · bailed on · bailed on

entries.meaning: To jump from an aircraft, or to get out of a situation before it goes bad. ---
examples: The pilot bailed out just before the crash.
He bails out whenever the work gets hard.
Two investors have bailed out since Tuesday.
entries.русский: выпрыгивать с парашютом, выпрыгнуть; сматываться, смотаться
entries.separable: no object — bail out; what you escape takes of: bail out of the deal
entries.forms: bail out · bailed out · bailed out

entries.meaning: To rescue a person or a company from trouble, usually with money. ---
examples: The government bailed out the banks.
My parents bailed me out again.
Nobody is going to bail this company out.
entries.separable: separable — bail out the airline, and bail them out
entries.forms: bail out · bailed out · bailed out

entries.meaning: To make two opposite things equal, or to become equal. ---
examples: The extra shifts balance out the slow weeks.
It all balanced out in the end.
The two costs are balancing each other out.
entries.separable: separable when it has an object — balance out the loss, balance it out; it also works with none: it all balanced out
entries.forms: balance out · balanced out · balanced out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (balance out the cost), intransitive (it balances out)

entries.meaning: To join with other people in order to act as a group. ---
examples: The neighbors banded together to fight the permit.
Small growers are banding together.
When money is tight, families band together.
entries.separable: no object — band together; who you join takes with: band together with the other tenants
entries.forms: band together · banded together · banded together

entries.meaning: To produce something quickly and without much care. ---
examples: She banged out the report in an hour.
He bangs out three songs a week.
I'm banging out an email and then we can go.
entries.русский: строчить, настрочить; быстро делать, быстро сделать
entries.separable: separable — bang out a draft, and bang it out
entries.forms: bang out · banged out · banged out

entries.meaning: To damage something, or injure a part of the body, by hitting it. ---
examples: He banged up the car in the parking garage.
She bangs her knee up on that shelf every single week.
The rental was already banged up when we got it.
entries.separable: separable — bang up the fender, and bang it up
entries.forms: bang up · banged up · banged up

entries.meaning: To depend on something happening. ---
examples: Don't bank on the weather holding.
We banked on a quiet summer and got the opposite.
They're banking on him to close the deal.
entries.separable: inseparable — bank on a raise, never ✗ bank a raise on
entries.forms: bank on · banked on · banked on

entries.meaning: To expect something, almost always in a sentence saying you did not. ---
examples: That was more than I bargained for.
She got more trouble than she had bargained for.
Nobody bargains for a flat tire in the rain.
entries.русский: ожидать, ожидать заранее; предвидеть, предвидеть заранее
entries.separable: inseparable — bargain for trouble, never ✗ bargain trouble for; it lives mostly in the phrase more than I bargained for
entries.forms: bargain for · bargained for · bargained for

entries.meaning: To enter or interrupt rudely, without being invited. ---
examples: He barged in without knocking.
She barges in whenever she feels like it.
Sorry for barging in on your call.
entries.separable: no object — barge in; what you interrupt takes on: barge in on a meeting
entries.forms: barge in · barged in · barged in

entries.meaning: To discuss an idea informally, without deciding anything yet. ---
examples: Let's bat around a few names for the new shop.
We batted the idea around for an hour and got nowhere.
They're still batting around possible dates for the trip.
entries.separable: separable — bat around a few ideas, or bat a few ideas around; with a pronoun it must split: bat it around
entries.forms: bat around · batted around · batted around

entries.meaning: To scold someone loudly and angrily. ---
examples: The coach bawled him out in front of everyone.
She bawls out the whole crew when the orders are late.
I got bawled out for being ten minutes late.
entries.separable: separable — bawl out the kid, and bawl him out
entries.forms: bawl out · bawled out · bawled out

entries.meaning: To make something stronger, bigger, or more effective. ---
examples: They beefed up security after the break-in.
We need to beef the ending up.
The airline is beefing up its winter schedule.
entries.separable: separable — beef up the staff, and beef it up
entries.forms: beef up · beefed up · beefed up

entries.meaning: To politely get out of something you had already agreed to do. ---
examples: He said he'd come, then begged off at the last minute.
I had to beg off the dinner because of work.
She has begged off three weekends in a row.
entries.русский: отказываться, отказаться (от приглашения, обязательства); отпрашиваться, отпроситься
entries.separable: inseparable — beg off the meeting, never ✗ beg the meeting off; most often it takes no object at all: he begged off
entries.forms: beg off · begged off · begged off
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (she begged off), transitive (he begged off the trip)

entries.meaning: To sing or play something very loudly. ---
examples: She belted out the national anthem.
He belts out show tunes in the shower.
The band was belting out an old Motown number.
entries.русский: петь во весь голос, спеть во весь голос; горланить
entries.separable: separable — belt out a song, and belt it out
entries.forms: belt out · belted out · belted out

entries.meaning: To cover written words with ink so that they cannot be read. ---
examples: The agency blacked out every name in the file.
Someone had blacked the address out with a marker.
They're blacking out the sensitive parts before release.
entries.separable: separable — black out the names, and black them out
entries.forms: black out · blacked out · blacked out

entries.meaning: To cut the power to a place, or to make it completely dark. ---
examples: The storm blacked out half the county.
They're blacking the windows out for the show.
Three neighborhoods were blacked out until Tuesday.
entries.separable: separable — black out the city, and black it out
entries.forms: black out · blacked out · blacked out

entries.meaning: To lose consciousness, or to lose all memory of a period of time. ---
examples: He blacked out for a few seconds.
I black out if I stand up too fast.
She had blacked out before the ambulance arrived.
entries.русский: терять сознание, потерять сознание; отключаться, отключиться
entries.separable: no object — black out; there is nothing to place between the two words
entries.forms: black out · blacked out · blacked out

entries.meaning: To suddenly be unable to remember something you know. ---
examples: I blanked out in the middle of the exam.
She blanks out whenever someone raises their voice.
He was blanking out on her name the whole evening.
entries.русский: забывать начисто, забыть начисто; отключаться, отключиться
entries.separable: no object — blank out; what you cannot recall takes on: blank out on her name
entries.forms: blank out · blanked out · blanked out

entries.meaning: For a rocket to leave the ground. ---
examples: The rocket blasted off at dawn.
The shuttle blasts off on Thursday.
We watched it blast off from the beach.
entries.separable: no object — blast off; nothing can sit between the two words
entries.forms: blast off · blasted off · blasted off

entries.meaning: To look or behave enough like everything around you that nobody notices you. ---
examples: He tried to blend in with the locals.
The new couch blends in nicely.
She was blending in until she opened her mouth.
entries.separable: no object — blend in; what you match takes with: blend in with the crowd
entries.forms: blend in · blended in · blended in

entries.meaning: To park so close to another car that it cannot get out. ---
examples: Somebody blocked me in again.
A delivery truck blocks in the whole row every morning.
We were blocked in until the driver came back.
entries.separable: separable — block in a car, and block it in; with a pronoun it must split: they blocked me in
entries.forms: block in · blocked in · blocked in

entries.meaning: To close an area so that nobody can get through it. ---
examples: Police blocked off the street.
They're blocking off the whole block for the parade.
We blocked the stairs off with a baby gate.
entries.separable: separable — block off the road, and block it off
entries.forms: block off · blocked off · blocked off

entries.meaning: To set aside a period of time for one purpose. ---
examples: Block out two hours for the review.
I blocked Friday morning out for the move.
She's blocking out time to write.
entries.separable: separable — block out an afternoon, and block it out
entries.forms: block out · blocked out · blocked out

entries.meaning: To stop light, noise, or an unwanted thought from getting through. ---
examples: Heavy curtains block out the light.
She blocked out the noise with headphones.
He has blocked out most of that year.
entries.separable: separable — block out the sun, and block it out
entries.forms: block out · blocked out · blocked out

entries.meaning: To hide something completely from sight, or to push a memory out of your mind. ---
examples: Clouds blotted out the sun.
He tries to blot out the memory with work.
The smoke was blotting out the whole ridge.
entries.русский: заслонять, заслонить; стирать из памяти, стереть
entries.separable: separable — blot out the light, and blot it out
entries.forms: blot out · blotted out · blotted out

entries.meaning: To say something suddenly, without stopping to think. ---
examples: She blurted out the price before he could stop her.
He blurts out whatever he's thinking.
I didn't mean to, but I blurted it out.
entries.separable: separable — blurt out the answer, and blurt it out
entries.forms: blurt out · blurted out · blurted out

entries.meaning: To cover a window or door with boards to protect or close a building. ---
examples: They boarded up the windows before the storm.
The store has been boarded up for years.
He's boarding the place up this weekend.
entries.separable: separable — board up the door, and board it up
entries.forms: board up · boarded up · boarded up

entries.meaning: To get stuck in detail or difficulty so that no progress is made. ---
examples: The talks bogged down over money.
Don't let the details bog you down.
The project has bogged down completely.
entries.separable: separable when it has an object — bog the team down, bog down the team; often there is none: the project bogged down
entries.forms: bog down · bogged down · bogged down
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (the talks bogged down), transitive (the paperwork bogged us down)

entries.meaning: To disappear completely by turning to steam. ---
examples: Turn the heat up and boil the extra liquid away.
Half the stock had boiled away by the time I came back.
The last of the water is boiling away now.
entries.русский: выкипать, выкипеть; испаряться, испариться при кипении
entries.separable: separable when it takes an object — boil away the liquid, boil the liquid away; most often it takes none: the water boiled away
entries.forms: boil away · boiled away · boiled away
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (the water boiled away), transitive (boil the extra liquid away)

entries.meaning: To cook a liquid until much of it evaporates and what is left is thicker. ---
examples: Boil down the syrup until it coats the back of a spoon.
She boiled the cream down by half.
The sauce has been boiling down for twenty minutes.
entries.separable: separable — boil down the sauce, or boil the sauce down; with a pronoun it must split: boil it down
entries.forms: boil down · boiled down · boiled down

entries.meaning: To shorten a long piece of writing or speech to its main points. ---
examples: Can you boil down this report for the board?
He boiled the whole argument down into three sentences.
I've boiled down my notes for you.
entries.separable: separable — boil down the report, or boil the report down; with a pronoun it must split: boil it down
entries.forms: boil down · boiled down · boiled down

entries.meaning: To have one simple thing as the real point, once everything else is stripped away. ---
examples: It all boils down to money.
The argument boiled down to one word.
What it's boiling down to is a question of trust.
entries.separable: inseparable — nothing can split the three words: it boils down to money, never ✗ it boils money down to
entries.forms: boil down to · boiled down to · boiled down to
entries.third person: boils down to · -ing form: boiling down to

entries.meaning: For anger or tension to break out into open conflict. ---
examples: The argument boiled over in the parking lot.
Tensions boil over every August.
Things had been boiling over long before anyone called the police.
entries.русский: вскипать, вскипеть; перерастать в скандал, перерасти
entries.separable: no object — boil over; there is nothing to place between the two words
entries.forms: boil over · boiled over · boiled over

entries.meaning: For a strong feeling or a quarrel to grow and rise until it is hard to hold in. ---
examples: She could feel the anger boil up again.
Resentment boiled up between the two departments.
Something has been boiling up in that office for months.
entries.separable: inseparable — the feeling is the subject, not an object: anger boiled up in him, never ✗ boil anger up
entries.forms: boil up · boiled up · boiled up

entries.meaning: To fail badly and drop out of something, especially a contest. ---
examples: He bombed out in the first round of the tournament.
If we bomb out here, the season is over.
Two of the favorites have bombed out already.
entries.separable: inseparable — bomb out of the first round, never ✗ bomb the round out
entries.forms: bomb out · bombed out · bombed out

entries.meaning: To study a subject hard in a short time, usually before a test or a meeting. ---
examples: I need to bone up on my Spanish before the trip.
He boned up on tax law over the weekend.
She's boning up on the case files tonight.
entries.separable: inseparable — bone up on the rules, never ✗ bone the rules up on
entries.forms: bone up on · boned up on · boned up on
entries.third person: bones up on · -ing form: boning up on

entries.meaning: To force someone to leave a job, a school, or a place. ---
examples: The board booted him out in March.

entries.separable: no object — intransitive; what you are dodging follows of: cop out of the interview, never ✗ cop the interview out.
entries.forms: cop out · copped out · copped out

entries.meaning: To write down exactly what someone says or what is written somewhere else. ---
examples: Copy down the homework before the bell rings.
I copied the phone number down wrong.
He was copying down everything the professor said.
entries.separable: separable — copy down the address, and copy the address down; with a pronoun it must split: copy it down.
entries.forms: copy down · copied down · copied down

entries.meaning: To close off an area with barriers or tape so that people cannot enter. ---
examples: Police cordoned off two blocks around the building.
They're cordoning off the street for the parade.
The whole wing gets cordoned off during the inspection.
entries.separable: separable — cordon off the street, and cordon the street off; with a pronoun it must split: cordon it off.
entries.forms: cordon off · cordoned off · cordoned off

entries.meaning: To take a liking to someone, or to warm to an idea. ---
examples: The neighbors never cottoned to the new fence.
He does not cotton to being told what to do.
Investors have not cottoned to the idea at all.
entries.русский: проникаться симпатией, проникнуться (к кому-л.); одобрять, одобрить (идею)
entries.separable: inseparable — what you take to follows to: cotton to the idea, never ✗ cotton the idea to.
entries.forms: cotton to · cottoned to · cottoned to

entries.meaning: To hand over money or information that you did not want to give. ---
examples: We had to cough up two hundred dollars for the tow.
He finally coughed up the name of his supplier.
Nobody enjoys coughing up extra fees at checkout.
entries.separable: separable — cough up the money, and cough the money up; with a pronoun it must split: cough it up.
entries.forms: cough up · coughed up · coughed up

entries.meaning: To be treated as a mark against someone who is being judged. ---
examples: A gap in your résumé should not count against you.
The late payments counted against her loan application.
Two missed shifts have already counted against his review.
entries.русский: идти в минус, быть минусом; вредить, повредить (при оценке)
entries.separable: inseparable — the person it hurts follows against: counted against him, never ✗ counted him against.
entries.forms: count against · counted against · counted against

entries.meaning: To count backward toward a moment you are waiting for. ---
examples: The crowd counted down from ten.
We're counting down the days until the trip.
She counts down to Friday every single week.
entries.separable: mostly intransitive with to — count down to New Year's; with an object it can split (count the days down), though count down the days is far commoner.
entries.forms: count down · counted down · counted down
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (count down to midnight), transitive (count down the days)

entries.meaning: To include someone in a plan or activity. ---
examples: If you're ordering pizza, count me in.
They counted us in without even asking.
He's counting everyone in for Saturday's game.
entries.separable: separable, and it normally splits — count me in, count Dave in; ✗ count in me is impossible.
entries.forms: count in · counted in · counted in

entries.meaning: To decide that someone has no chance of winning or succeeding. ---
examples: Don't count him out — he's come back from worse.
Everyone had counted the team out by halftime.
You'd be counting her out far too early.
entries.русский: сбрасывать со счетов, сбросить со счетов
entries.separable: separable, and it normally splits — don't count her out; ✗ count out her is impossible.
entries.forms: count out · counted out · counted out

entries.meaning: To leave someone out of a plan or activity. ---
examples: If it starts before seven, count me out.
They counted him out of the weekend trip.
She's counting herself out of the potluck this time.
entries.separable: separable, and it normally splits — count me out, count him out; ✗ count out me is impossible.
entries.forms: count out · counted out · counted out

entries.meaning: To add together everything in a group to get a total. ---
examples: Count up the votes and tell me the total.
He counted up what he had spent and winced.
I'm counting the receipts up now.
entries.separable: separable — count up the votes, and count the votes up; with a pronoun it must split: count them up.
entries.forms: count up · counted up · counted up

entries.meaning: To do someone's job for them while they are away. ---
examples: Can you cover for me on Friday?
She covered for her boss all through August.
Who's covering for the front desk at lunch?
entries.separable: inseparable — cover for me, never ✗ cover me for; the person always follows for.
entries.forms: cover for · covered for · covered for

entries.meaning: To lie or hide the truth in order to protect someone who has done something wrong. ---
examples: His partner covered for him for years.
Don't ask me to cover for you again.
She has been covering for her brother since high school.
entries.separable: inseparable — cover for your brother, never ✗ cover your brother for.
entries.forms: cover for · covered for · covered for

entries.meaning: To hide a mistake, a crime, or an embarrassing fact so that others do not find out. ---
examples: The company tried to cover up the spill.
They covered it up for almost a decade.
He's terrible at covering up how he feels.
entries.separable: separable — cover up the mistake, and cover the mistake up; with a pronoun it must split: cover it up.
entries.forms: cover up · covered up · covered up

entries.meaning: To put on more clothing, or to put cloth over part of the body. ---
examples: Cover up — it's thirty degrees out there.
She covered her shoulders up before going into the church.
He was covering up the sunburn with a long-sleeved shirt.
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — cover up your arms, cover them up; just as often there is no object: cover up, it's cold.
entries.forms: cover up · covered up · covered up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (cover up your arms), intransitive (cover up, it's cold)

entries.meaning: To be very friendly to someone powerful in order to get something out of them. ---
examples: He's been cozying up to the new director all month.
The company cozied up to regulators for years.
She cozies up to whoever happens to be in charge.
entries.separable: inseparable — cozy up to the boss, never ✗ cozy the boss up to; the person always follows to.
entries.forms: cozy up to · cozied up to · cozied up to
entries.third person: cozies up to · -ing form: cozying up to

entries.meaning: To start dealing with bad behavior much more strictly. ---
examples: The city is cracking down on illegal parking.
Police cracked down hard after the second break-in.
Schools have cracked down on phones in class.
entries.русский: принимать жёсткие меры, принять; ужесточать борьбу (с)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the target follows on: crack down on speeding, never ✗ crack speeding down.
entries.forms: crack down · cracked down · cracked down

entries.meaning: To open a bottle, can, or container, especially a drink to enjoy. ---
examples: Let's crack open a bottle of wine.
He cracked a beer open and put his feet up.
They were cracking open sodas on the porch.
entries.separable: separable — crack open a beer, and crack a beer open; with a pronoun it must split: crack it open.
entries.forms: crack open · cracked open · cracked open

entries.meaning: To burst out laughing. ---
examples: The whole class cracked up.
I crack up every time I watch that scene.
She was cracking up before he even got to the punchline.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive in this sense: the whole room cracked up.
entries.forms: crack up · cracked up · cracked up

entries.meaning: To have a mental or emotional breakdown from stress. ---
examples: He nearly cracked up during finals week.
She's cracking up under the pressure of two jobs.
Two of them cracked up and quit before the season ended.
entries.русский: срываться, сорваться; не выдерживать, не выдержать (психически)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: he cracked up under the pressure.
entries.forms: crack up · cracked up · cracked up

entries.meaning: To make someone laugh a lot. ---
examples: That commercial cracks me up.
His impression of the boss cracked everyone up.
Stop — you're cracking me up.
entries.separable: separable, and it normally splits — that joke cracks me up; it cracked up the whole table is also fine, but a pronoun must sit in the middle: ✗ crack up me.
entries.forms: crack up · cracked up · cracked up

entries.meaning: To study very hard for a short time right before a test. ---
examples: He crammed for the exam all night.
She's cramming for finals in the library.
I always cram for tests and regret it afterward.
entries.separable: inseparable — cram for the test, never ✗ cram the test for; the exam always follows for.
entries.forms: cram for · crammed for · crammed for

entries.meaning: To fit more things or activities into a space or a period of time than it comfortably holds. ---
examples: We crammed in three museums before lunch.
He crams too much in on the first day of the trip.
They're cramming forty kids in one classroom.
entries.separable: separable — cram in three museums, and cram three museums in; with a pronoun it must split: cram them in.
entries.forms: cram in · crammed in · crammed in

entries.meaning: To produce something quickly and in large amounts, usually without much care. ---
examples: The plant cranks out a thousand units a day.
He cranked out three articles before noon.
She's been cranking out sketches all week.
entries.русский: штамповать, наштамповать; выдавать в большом количестве
entries.separable: separable — crank out a report, and crank a report out; with a pronoun it must split: crank them out.
entries.forms: crank out · cranked out · cranked out

entries.meaning: To increase the volume, heat, or intensity of something. ---
examples: Crank up the heat — I'm freezing.
He cranked the music up until the windows rattled.
They're cranking up production for the holidays.
entries.separable: separable — crank up the heat, and crank the heat up; with a pronoun it must split: crank it up.
entries.forms: crank up · cranked up · cranked up

entries.meaning: To start a machine or an engine. ---
examples: He cranked up the generator when the power went out.
I'll crank the grill up in a few minutes.
She was cranking up the old tractor when we pulled in.
entries.separable: separable — crank up the generator, and crank the generator up; with a pronoun it must split: crank it up.
entries.forms: crank up · cranked up · cranked up

entries.meaning: To fall asleep suddenly from exhaustion, usually not in your own bed. ---
examples: He crashed out on the couch with his shoes still on.
I will crash out the second we get back to the hotel.
Half the crew was crashing out in the van between shoots.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the place follows the whole phrase: crashed out on the couch.
entries.forms: crash out · crashed out · crashed out

entries.meaning: To appear or happen unexpectedly. ---
examples: A problem cropped up with the permits.
Her name crops up in every other chapter.
Little delays keep cropping up as we get closer to launch.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the thing that appears is the subject: a problem cropped up.
entries.forms: crop up · cropped up · cropped up

entries.meaning: To remove an item or a name from a list because it is done or no longer needed. ---
examples: Cross the milk off the list — I already bought it.
She crossed off three names before noon.
He's crossing chores off as he finishes them.
entries.separable: separable — cross off the milk, and cross the milk off; with a pronoun it must split: cross it off the list.
entries.forms: cross off · crossed off · crossed off

entries.meaning: To draw a line through something written because it is wrong or no longer wanted. ---
examples: Cross out the wrong answer and write the right one above it.
He crossed my name out with a red pen.
She had crossed out half the paragraph.
entries.separable: separable — cross out the wrong answer, and cross the wrong answer out; with a pronoun it must split: cross it out.
entries.forms: cross out · crossed out · crossed out

entries.meaning: To move from one side, group, or style to another. ---
examples: She crossed over from country music to pop.
Every year a few senators cross over to vote with the other party.
The show has crossed over to a much younger audience.
entries.русский: переходить, перейти (на другую сторону, в другой жанр)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; where you move to follows to or into: cross over to jazz.
entries.forms: cross over · crossed over · crossed over

entries.meaning: To take up so much room or attention that something else is left with none. ---
examples: The big chains crowded out the local bookstores.
Test prep is crowding art out of the school day.
Cheap imports have crowded out domestic makers.
entries.separable: separable — crowd out the small shops, and crowd the small shops out; with a pronoun it must split: crowd them out.
entries.forms: crowd out · crowded out · crowded out

entries.meaning: To make a loud sound suddenly because of pain, fear, or surprise. ---
examples: He cried out when the nurse touched his shoulder.
She cries out in her sleep sometimes.
Someone was crying out two floors below.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the reason follows in or with: cry out in pain.
entries.forms: cry out · cried out · cried out

entries.meaning: To need something so badly that the need is obvious to everyone. ---
examples: This kitchen is crying out for a coat of paint.
The system cried out for reform long before anyone acted.
Small towns like ours cry out for doctors.
entries.separable: inseparable — crying out for repairs, never ✗ cry repairs out for; what is needed always follows for.
entries.forms: cry out for · cried out for · cried out for
entries.third person: cries out for · -ing form: crying out for

entries.meaning: To lie or sit very close to someone for warmth or affection. ---
examples: The kids cuddled up under one blanket.
She cuddles up to the dog every night.
They were cuddling up on the couch watching a movie.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the person or animal follows to, with, or next to: cuddle up to the dog.
entries.forms: cuddle up · cuddled up · cuddled up

entries.meaning: To get a song, video, or clip ready so that it starts at the right moment. ---
examples: Cue up the next song.
He had already cued up the video before the meeting started.
She's cuing up the slides for the talk.
entries.русский: ставить на воспроизведение, поставить; готовить к запуску
entries.separable: separable — cue up the next song, and cue the next song up; with a pronoun it must split: cue it up.
entries.forms: cue up · cued up · cued up

entries.meaning: To settle into a comfortable position with your arms and legs pulled in close.
examples: She curled up with a book and a blanket.
The cat curls up on the warm laptop every afternoon.
He has curled up in that same chair every evening this week.
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; what you settle with follows with: curl up with a book.
entries.forms: curl up · curled up · curled up
